proposals.before: Jin chancellor Li Song had gone north with the Khitan. When the High Ancestor entered the capital he gave Song’s mansion to Fengji—and took Song’s fields and houses in the Western Capital as well.
proposals.after: Jin chancellor Li Song had gone north with the Khitan. When the High Ancestor entered the capital he gave Song’s mansion to Fengji; Song also had fields and houses in the Western Capital, and Fengji took those as well.
proposals.reason: Chinese 逢吉遂皆取之 makes Fengji, not the High Ancestor, take the Western Capital estates; the idiomatic sentence wrongly keeps the High Ancestor as subject.

proposals.before: Zhang Lingrou, Yanzhou’s bandit-hunter, then slaughtered several hundred people across seventeen villages in Pingyin County.
proposals.after: Zhang Lingrou, Yunzhou’s bandit-hunter, then slaughtered several hundred people across seventeen villages in Pingyin County.
proposals.reason: 鄆州 is Yunzhou; Yanzhou renders 兗州 and mistranslates the prefecture name.

proposals.before: Thereupon Zhang Lingrou, the Yanzhou bandit-capture envoy, killed altogether several hundred villagers of seventeen villages in Pingyin County.
proposals.after: Thereupon Zhang Lingrou, the Yunzhou bandit-capture envoy, killed altogether several hundred villagers of seventeen villages in Pingyin County.
proposals.reason: 鄆州 is Yunzhou; Yanzhou is the wrong place name.

proposals.before: Qianyou year two brought him the Grand Marshal’s seal.
proposals.after: In Qianyou year two he was additionally appointed Minister of Works.
proposals.reason: 司空 is Minister of Works (one of the Three Dukes), not Grand Marshal (太尉).

proposals.before: In the second year of Qianyou he was additionally appointed Grand Marshal.
proposals.after: In the second year of Qianyou he was additionally appointed Minister of Works.
proposals.reason: 司空 should not be rendered Grand Marshal.

proposals.before: Fengji spent the night in the eastern wing of the Jinxian Hall and told Wang Chune, the Summer Office director of astronomy: “Last night, before dusk, I saw Li Song beside me—the living keeping company with the dead. Nothing good can come of that.”
proposals.after: Fengji spent the night in the eastern wing of the Jinxiang Hall and told Wang Chune, the Summer Office director of astronomy: “Last night, before dusk, I saw Li Song beside me—the living keeping company with the dead. Nothing good can come of that.”
proposals.reason: 金祥殿 is Jinxiang Hall; Jinxian misreads 祥 as if 仙.

proposals.before: Fengji lodged by night in the eastern wing of the Jinxian Hall and said to Wang Chune, Director of the Directorate of Astronomy’s Summer Office: “Last night before dark I already saw Li Song at my side—the living meeting the dead: nothing auspicious.”
proposals.after: Fengji lodged by night in the eastern wing of the Jinxiang Hall and said to Wang Chune, Director of the Directorate of Astronomy’s Summer Office: “Last night before dark I already saw Li Song at my side—the living meeting the dead: nothing auspicious.”
proposals.reason: 金祥殿 is Jinxiang Hall; Jinxian misreads 祥 as if 仙.

proposals.before: In Liang’s last days seven households furnished one soldier. Hongzhao served under the Kaifeng circuit commander and was chosen for the palace guard.
proposals.after: In Liang’s last days seven households furnished one soldier. Hongzhao served in the Kaidao Command and was chosen for the palace guard.
proposals.reason: 開道指揮 names the Kaidao army command, not Kaifeng.

proposals.before: At the end of Liang, seven households were levied for one soldier; Hongzhao became a soldier, attached to the Kaifeng circuit commander, and was selected for the palace guard.
proposals.after: At the end of Liang, seven households were levied for one soldier; Hongzhao became a soldier, attached to the Kaidao Command, and was selected for the palace guard.
proposals.reason: 開道指揮 names the Kaidao army command, not Kaifeng.

proposals.before: Under the Deposed Emperor, Li Shouzhen of Hezhong, Wang Jingchong of Fengxiang, Zhao Sixian of Yongxing, and others rebelled. War opened in the western passes; fear ran through the realm. In the capital rumor fed rumor.
proposals.after: Under the Deposed Emperor, Li Shouzhen of Hezhong, Wang Jingchong of Fengxiang, Zhao Siwan of Yongxing, and others rebelled. War opened in the western passes; fear ran through the realm. In the capital rumor fed rumor.
proposals.reason: 趙思綰 is Zhao Siwan (綰 = wǎn), not Sixian.

proposals.before: In the Deposed Emperor’s time Li Shouzhen of Hezhong, Wang Jingchong of Fengxiang, Zhao Sixian of Yongxing, and others all rebelled. War was waged in the western passes; hearts were fearful. The people of the capital, by rumor, alarmed one another.
proposals.after: In the Deposed Emperor’s time Li Shouzhen of Hezhong, Wang Jingchong of Fengxiang, Zhao Siwan of Yongxing, and others all rebelled. War was waged in the western passes; hearts were fearful. The people of the capital, by rumor, alarmed one another.
proposals.reason: 趙思綰 is Zhao Siwan (綰 = wǎn), not Sixian.

proposals.before: He Yan Fujin of Yan had a jade pillow worth 140,000 cash; he sent a page to sell it in Huainan to trade for tea.
proposals.after: He Fujin of Yan had a jade pillow worth 140,000 cash; he sent a page to sell it in Huainan to trade for tea.
proposals.reason: 燕人何福進 is He Fujin of Yan; literal wrongly fuses place 燕 into the name.

proposals.before: Qu Wen of the Yongzhou yeast office and the officer He Zheng quarreled over duty and sued before the Three Departments, which ruled for Wen.
proposals.after: Qu Wen of the Yingzhou yeast office and the officer He Zheng quarreled over duty and sued before the Three Departments, which ruled for Wen.
proposals.reason: Chinese 潁州 is Yingzhou, not Yongzhou; the place name is mistranslated.

proposals.before: The Yongzhou yeast-works officer Qu Wen and the army officer He Zheng disputed official business and sued at the Three Departments; the Three Departments ruled for Wen.
proposals.after: The Yingzhou yeast-works officer Qu Wen and the army officer He Zheng disputed official business and sued at the Three Departments; the Three Departments ruled for Wen.
proposals.reason: Chinese 潁州 is Yingzhou, not Yongzhou; the place name is mistranslated.

proposals.before: When the western war ended the Deposed Emperor drifted toward petty favorites—Hou Zan, Li Ye, and the rest—and played without restraint. The dowager’s kin peddled influence; Hongzhao and Yang Bin checked them where they could.
proposals.after: When the western war ended the Hidden Emperor drifted toward petty favorites—Hou Zan, Li Ye, and the rest—and played without restraint. The dowager’s kin peddled influence; Hongzhao and Yang Bin checked them where they could.
proposals.reason: 隱帝 is the Hidden Emperor (Emperor Yin), not the Deposed Emperor (廢帝); the title is mistranslated.

proposals.before: At enthronement Zhang became Three Departments commissioner and Acting Grand General.
proposals.after: At enthronement Zhang became Three Departments commissioner and Acting Grand Commandant.
proposals.reason: 太尉 is Grand Commandant (or Defender-in-chief), not Grand General; the idiomatic rendering misnames the office.

proposals.before: The High Ancestor died; the Hidden Emperor made Zhang Grand General and Associate Grand Councilor.
proposals.after: The High Ancestor died; the Hidden Emperor made Zhang Grand Commandant and Associate Grand Councilor.
proposals.reason: 太尉 is Grand Commandant, not Grand General; same office mistranslation as in the prior unit.

proposals.before: Guo Wei meant to win hearts and asked his ministers: “Vice Director Liu fell hard from his horse; soldiers humiliated him, yet he lives. I would ask the dowager to spare his family—what say you?”
proposals.after: Guo Wei meant to win hearts and asked his ministers: “Palace Attendant Liu fell hard from his horse; soldiers humiliated him, yet he lives. I would ask the dowager to spare his family—what say you?”
proposals.reason: 劉侍中 is Palace Attendant Liu; 侍中 was already rendered Palace Attendant in this biography and is not Vice Director.

proposals.before: At that time Taizu wished to win hearts and discussed with his ministers: “Vice Director Liu fell from his horse and was badly hurt; soldiers pressed and humiliated him, yet he barely lives. I wish to memorialize the dowager and spare his household—what do you think?”
proposals.after: At that time Taizu wished to win hearts and discussed with his ministers: “Palace Attendant Liu fell from his horse and was badly hurt; soldiers pressed and humiliated him, yet he barely lives. I wish to memorialize the dowager and spare his household—what do you think?”
proposals.reason: Same 侍中 mistranslation as in the idiomatic field; align with Palace Attendant.

proposals.before: He stayed Zhu’s death. Li Ye and the rest were exposed in the market; their wives and children were spared.
proposals.after: He then killed only Zhu; Zhu, with Li Ye and the rest, had their heads exposed in the market, and their wives and children were pardoned.
proposals.reason: 止殺銖 means the killing stopped at Zhu (family spared), not that Zhu was spared; 與李業等梟首於市 states Zhu was beheaded with Li Ye and others.

proposals.before: He then stayed Zhu’s execution and, with Li Ye and the rest, exposed their heads in the market; their wives and children were pardoned.
proposals.after: He then limited the killing to Zhu and, with Li Ye and the rest, exposed their heads in the market; their wives and children were pardoned.
proposals.reason: Literal ‘stayed Zhu’s execution’ reverses 止殺銖; Zhu was executed and exposed, while wives and children were pardoned.

proposals.before: Li Ye was brother to the High Ancestor’s empress.
proposals.after: Li Ye was the younger brother of the High Ancestor’s empress.
proposals.reason: Chinese 弟 means younger brother; the idiomatic gloss omits the younger-brother sense that the literal preserves.

proposals.before: Guo Wei rebelled. The emperor sent Yuan Gui and Yan Jinqing against him at Chanyuan.
proposals.after: Guo Wei rebelled. The emperor sent Yuan Xue and Yan Jinqing against him at Chanyuan.
proposals.reason: The personal name 泬 is read Xuè, not Gui; the idiomatic romanization Yuan Gui mistranscribes 袁泬.

proposals.before: Wei raised troops in rebellion. The Hidden Emperor sent Left Divine Martial Commander Yuan Gui, Palace Horse Guard Commander Yan Jinqing, and the rest to lead troops against Wei at Chanyuan.
proposals.after: Wei raised troops in rebellion. The Hidden Emperor sent Left Divine Martial Commander Yuan Xue, Palace Horse Guard Commander Yan Jinqing, and the rest to lead troops against Wei at Chanyuan.
proposals.reason: Same romanization error for 袁泬 (Xuè) as in the idiomatic field; at most one repair per unit and field so both fields need separate rows.

proposals.before: Han fell at the northern suburb. Ye stuffed the inner treasury’s gold into his robes and fled to his brother Hongxin at Baoyi; Hongxin turned him away.
proposals.after: When Han’s army was defeated at the northern suburb, Ye stuffed the inner treasury’s gold into his robes and fled to his brother Hongxin at Baoyi; Hongxin turned him away.
proposals.reason: 漢兵敗 means the Han army was defeated, not that Han as a polity fell; the idiomatic wording invents a dynastic collapse reading.

proposals.before: Guo Yunming was raised a steward in the Han High Ancestor’s household. The High Ancestor favored him and made him Hanlin Commissioner of Tea and Wine.
proposals.after: Guo Yunming had from youth been a steward in the Han High Ancestor’s household. The High Ancestor favored him and made him Hanlin Commissioner of Tea and Wine.
proposals.reason: Chinese 少為…廝養 means he served as a household steward from youth, not that he was ‘raised a steward’; the idiomatic English is ambiguous and slightly invents a rearing sense.

proposals.before: All Jingnan trembled. Baorong paid him off handsomely to see him gone.
proposals.after: The people of Jingnan were all terrified. Baorong paid him off handsomely to see him gone.
proposals.reason: 荊人皆恐 refers to the Jingnan populace’s fear, not a personified ‘All Jingnan’; the literal field already renders the people correctly.

decisions.reason: Focus unit gives Song’s mansion by the High Ancestor (以崧第賜逢吉) then states Song also had Western Capital estates and 逢吉遂皆取之; the before text wrongly keeps the High Ancestor as subject of the seizure, and the after correctly assigns it to Fengji.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 而崧別有田宅在西京，逢吉遂皆取之

decisions.reason: Focus unit names 鄆州捕賊使者; 鄆州 is Yunzhou, so Yanzhou (兗州) is a wrong place name and Yunzhou is the accurate repair.
The literal field has the same error: 鄆州 must be Yunzhou, not Yanzhou.
Focus unit says 加拜司空; 司空 is Minister of Works, not Grand Marshal (太尉), and the after correctly renders the additional appointment.
The literal field likewise misrenders 司空 as Grand Marshal; Minister of Works matches the Chinese.
Focus unit has 金祥殿; 祥 is xiang, so Jinxiang Hall is correct and Jinxian wrongly reads the graph as if 仙.
The literal field has the same hall-name error; 金祥殿 is Jinxiang Hall, not Jinxian Hall.
Focus unit attaches Hongzhao to 開道指揮; that is the Kaidao Command, not a Kaifeng circuit commander.
The literal field likewise invents Kaifeng for 開道指揮; Kaidao Command matches the Chinese unit name.
Focus unit names 趙思綰; 綰 is wǎn, so Zhao Siwan is correct and Sixian is a false reading of the given name.
The literal field has the same romanization error for 趙思綰; Zhao Siwan restores the correct reading.
Focus unit says 燕人何福進: 燕人 marks origin and 何福進 is the name; “He Yan Fujin” wrongly folds the place into the personal name, and He Fujin of Yan is accurate.
Focus unit has 潁州麹場官; 潁州 is Yingzhou, so Yongzhou is a wrong prefecture name.
The literal field likewise misrenders 潁州 as Yongzhou; Yingzhou matches the Chinese and the following unit’s Ying.
Focus unit names 隱帝; that is the Hidden Emperor (Emperor Yin), not the Deposed Emperor (廢帝), so the title repair is required.
Focus unit has 檢校太尉; 太尉 is Grand Commandant, not Grand General, and Acting Grand Commandant matches 檢校太尉.
Focus unit adds 太尉; the same office must be Grand Commandant, not Grand General.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 加太尉、同中書門下平章事

decisions.reason: The quoted title is 劉侍中; 侍中 is Palace Attendant, not Vice Director, so Palace Attendant Liu is the correct repair.
The literal field has the same 侍中 error; Palace Attendant Liu matches the Chinese title.

Focus unit 乃止殺銖，與李業等梟首於市，赦其妻子 means the killing was limited to Zhu, who was beheaded and exposed with Li Ye and the rest while wives and children were pardoned; “stayed Zhu’s death” reverses the sense, and the after restores it.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 乃止殺銖，與李業等梟首於市，赦其妻子

decisions.reason: The literal “stayed Zhu’s execution” likewise reverses 止殺銖; limiting the killing to Zhu and exposing heads with Li Ye matches the Chinese.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 乃止殺銖，與李業等梟首於市，赦其妻子

decisions.reason: Focus unit says 高祖皇后之弟; 弟 is specifically younger brother, and the following unit confirms Ye was youngest, so omitting “younger” drops kinship specificity the Chinese marks.
Focus unit names 袁泬; 泬 is read Xuè, so Yuan Xue is correct and Yuan Gui is a false romanization.
The literal field has the same error for 袁泬; Yuan Xue restores the correct reading of 泬.
Focus unit says 漢兵敗於北郊: the Han army was defeated, not that the Han polity fell; the after removes the invented dynastic-collapse reading.
Focus unit 少為漢高祖廝養 means he served as a household steward from youth; “was raised a steward” invents a rearing sense the Chinese does not have, and the after matches 少為.
荊人皆恐 is adequately rendered by the literary metonymy “All Jingnan trembled”; shifting to “The people of Jingnan were all terrified” is a stylistic preference that does not correct a semantic error.

claimRetractions.reason: Accepting r0015 shows English “Deposed Emperor” for 隱帝 came only from the bad idiomatic; the correct title claim remains c0191 Hidden Emperor.

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0010 shows English Zhao Sixian came from misreading 綰; the personal-name claim must read Zhao Siwan while keeping zh, pinyin, id, subject, predicate, certainty, and evidence.
Accepted r0023 shows English Yuan Gui came from a false reading of 泬; the personal-name claim must read Yuan Xue while keeping zh, id, subject, predicate, certainty, and evidence.
